root_causes: The initial tiny corpus did not provide PostgreSQL planner statistics or a cost crossover that could discriminate HNSW and GIN eligibility.
A standalone search_vector GIN competed with a tenant/dictionary B-tree in the RLS-protected joined query shape instead of covering the authorization and lexical predicates together.
The bounded planner fixture used colon-prefixed SQL string literals that SQLAlchemy text parsing treated as bind names.
The multi-tenant regression fixture reused one globally unique embedding model UUID across tenants.
excluded_paths: vector or lexical result mismatch before planner-only corpus inflation
repair: Add bounded deterministic planner data and refresh statistics after the build.
Use a composite tenant_id/dictionary_version/search_vector GIN backed by PostgreSQL btree_gin, while retaining the B-tree for non-FTS tenant operations.
Keep the GIN eligibility probe separate from normal retrieval, restore planner settings after EXPLAIN, and benchmark the unforced production query.
Replace ambiguous colon literals and derive stable per-tenant model UUIDs.

pgvector.installation: 38 previously absent extension files copied into the isolated local PostgreSQL 17 installation; no existing file was overwritten

rollback: Revert the P11-004 files and remove only the hash-verified extension files added to the isolated local test installation; schema and production state remain unchanged.
